newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: OLD MUTUAL KEEN TO INVEST MORE IN NAMIBIA.
newsitem.headline: OLD MUTUAL KEEN TO INVEST MORE IN NAMIBIA.

text.p: Old Mutual was keen to further invest in Namibian equities, following the success of the Namibian Stock Exchange (NSE), a company official said on Tuesday.
Old Mutual's Growth Fund porfolio manager Alwyn van der Merwe told Reuters the growth outlook for both the Namibian and South African stock markets was also encouraging.

"One only has to glance at the number of companies listed on the NSE over the past two years and the huge jump in the value of shares traded from around 239 million Namibian dollars ($54 million) to over 660 million Namibian dollars to realise that the exchange is now established as one of Africa's foremost share markets," van der Merwe said.

Old Mutual's Nambian Growth Fund achieved the fourth highest return of 21 percent out of all Namibian and South African general equity unit trusts in the 12 months ended March 1997, and has risen from seven million Namibian dollars to 36.9 million in 32 months.

Currently just over 10 percent of the fund's portfolio is invested in Namibian equities, namely in De Beers (3.66 percent, dual-listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange), First National Bank Namibia (1.99 percent), Namibia Breweries (1.9 percent), CIC Holdings (1.9 percent), Namsea and Namfish (0.5 percent), Sentra Namibia (0.25 percent).

Van der Merwe said with interest rates in both Namibia and South Africa at their peaks and an upturn in corporate earnings likely next year -- on a 12 to 18 months view -- prospects for renewed growth in share prices were excellent.

He said while there was some nervousness over the trend of the New York stock market and in U.S. interest rates, he did not view either of the two as a major threat, because "the Namibian and the South African markets reflect value relative to the U.S. markets and are thus less vulnerable should Wall Street come under pressure".
